locator: Human feedback on decision processes; warning about fooling the interface
finding: Proposes internal-process feedback and explicitly anticipates optimizing appearances instead of the intended property.
scope: Research motivation, not a quantitative forecast or deadline.

locator: Catching problems with auditing; Deliberate design; What if interpretability breaks down
finding: Describes systematic auditing, deliberate design and strong reverse engineering as safety routes.
scope: Hubinger's account of discussions with Olah, not a verbatim manifesto or dated delivery commitment.

finding: Proposes understandable features and circuits, including directions rather than only individual neurons.
scope: Speculative scientific claims; examples principally from vision models.

finding: Dictionary learning recovers features in a small transformer that are obscured in individual neurons.
scope: A useful decomposition is not evidence of complete safety coverage.

locator: Discussion: Getting All the Features and Compute
finding: Feature extraction reaches Claude 3 Sonnet; authors do not know the total feature count and expect major omissions.
scope: One selected layer; no denominator for completeness.

finding: Representation rerouting reduces harmful outputs and actions in evaluated attack settings.
scope: Broad internal-access safety method; not a complete mechanistic explanation.

finding: Revised continuous embedding attacks achieve reported 100% attack success against tested circuit-breaker models.
scope: Powerful embedding-space access, not an ordinary text-only attack; does not invalidate all original threat settings.

finding: Apparently clean SAE features miss expected cases because concepts are absorbed into other features; changing size or sparsity is insufficient in the tested setting.
scope: First-letter identification with known labels; not a direct catastrophe-risk test.

finding: Optimized attacks evade latent monitors, including tests on models trained with internal defenses; harder tasks can impose an obfuscation cost.
scope: Attacker access and tasks vary. Not evidence that every internal defense fails.

finding: Practical SAE metrics need not track reconstruction proxies; extended absorption measurement captures partial and distributed failures.
scope: Benchmark protocol changes prevent treating old and new absorption scores as a fixed historical series.

date_basis: arXiv v1; earlier informal work exists
finding: Nested dictionaries avoid absorption in a toy setup and reduce it on tested language models; five nested objectives add about 50% training time.
scope: Repair within tested settings, not complete concept recovery. The publication date is not the repair's first availability.

finding: Three of four teams find a hidden objective; all three successful teams have training-data access, and one uses no SAE tools.
scope: One model organism; access differences prevent attributing the team success gap to interpretability.

finding: On the benchmark's causal-variable localization tasks, SAEs do not outperform neurons; supervised DAS performs best.
scope: Different tasks and models, not a direct failed replication of Matryoshka or Sonnet feature discovery.

date_basis: arXiv v1; earlier public announcement exists
finding: Sparse-weight models yield understandable task circuits; preserving interpretability beyond tens of millions of nonzero parameters remains challenging.
scope: Capability and interpretability trade off; larger models improve the tested frontier.

finding: Training evasion of benign probes transfers to unseen safety probes fitted after the actor is frozen.
scope: Constructed model organisms with explicit triggers; not a finding that spontaneous evasion is inevitable.

locator: Producing Sparse Interpretable Circuits; faithfulness experiments
finding: Replicates much of the smaller-circuit advantage, but extracted circuits can repurpose nodes and fail under small distribution changes.
scope: Uses zero ablation for most experiments instead of the original mean ablation; not an exact refutation of every original circuit.

finding: Standardized audits of 56 models show strongest overall performance from scaffolded behavioral tools and a gap between tool evidence and agent success.
scope: 14 implanted behaviors and four training configurations; not a representative sample of future dangerous objectives.

finding: IA-equipped audits score 59% versus 53% for the prior best method on AuditBench. Separate tests still miss a core objective and specific sandbagging conditions.
scope: Same benchmark protocol, not equal total development cost. Success allows any of ten predictions; no deployment false-positive guarantee.

kind: direct challenge under additional attacker access
finding: Behavior-preserving weight transformations reduce reported IA detection from 100% to 0-20% on seven published fine-tunes.
scope: Malicious supplier controls weights before auditing; different subset, adapter and metric from the 59% AuditBench result. Not an across-the-board reversal.

finding: Hard and soft absorption complicate feature hierarchies in an evaluation on visual data.
scope: Different modality and protocol; cannot label this a failed replication of language-model Matryoshka results.

finding: Held-out tests support short functional descriptions for 12-31% of weights in the tested sparse transformers, exceeding tested dense models.
scope: Description-based ablation metric, not fraction of behavior or safety understood; not proof that the remaining weights are uninterpretable.

finding: Task-specific self-report training supplies signal in settings missed by transferred IAs.
scope: Requires target training data and per-target training; different tasks and judge limitations. Not a demonstrated repair of symmetry attacks.

finding: Frozen probe objectives can be exploited; updating probes improves tested harmlessness and honesty while preserving linear detectability.
scope: Models of 7B-14B; stronger optimization remains open. Not a matched retest of every earlier obfuscation attack.

finding: Activation replay reduces SAE activation-storage needs by 8-64 times with negligible loss on the evaluated quality metrics.
scope: Recent author-reported result; storage reduction is not an equivalent reduction in total interpretability cost or safety uncertainty.
